name: Vyākarana
description: While there has been significant progress towards developing NLU resources for Indic languages, syntactic evaluation has been relatively less explored. Unlike English, Indic languages have rich morphosyntax, grammatical genders, free linear word-order, and highly inflectional morphology. In this paper, we introduce Vyākarana: a benchmark of Colorless Green sentences in Indic languages for syntactic evaluation of multilingual language models. The benchmark comprises four syntax-related tasks: PoS Tagging, Syntax Tree-depth Prediction, Grammatical Case Marking, and Subject-Verb Agreement. We use the datasets from the evaluation tasks to probe five multilingual language models of varying architectures for syntax in Indic languages. Due to its prevalence, we also include a code-switching setting in our experiments. reputation: A specialized benchmark for probing syntactic knowledge in Indic languages that is useful in multilingual NLP research but not widely used as a mainstream leaderboard benchmark.
notes: Probe-style benchmark with relatively small, synthetic colorless green sentence data; results are task- and language-dependent and not directly comparable to broad NLU benchmarks.
